# Blender glTF Pipeline

Models are generated by a Python script, so they are reviewable, repeatable and licence-clean.

## Setup

- Use the current Blender **LTS** portable zip (download.blender.org/release/BlenderX.Y/…-windows-x64.zip), unpacked outside the repositories. Point the build at it with an env var (e.g. `BLENDER`).
- Run headless: `blender --background --factory-startup --python blender/build_assets.py -- <outDir>`.
- In the portable build, `bpy.ops.object.shade_auto_smooth` fails (it needs a bundled geometry-nodes asset). Use `bpy.ops.object.shade_smooth_by_angle(angle=…)`.

## Modelling patterns

- Helpers: `box(name, size, location, material, bevel)`, `cylinder(...)`, `lathe(name, profile, ...)` using `bmesh.ops.spin` for insulators/bushings, `join(name, objects)`, `parent(child, parent)`.
- Apply modifiers (bevel) before export for crisp edges and good highlights.
- **Animated parts**: separate object with a clear name (`Door`, `Breaker`) and the origin set to the pivot (`origin_set(type="ORIGIN_CURSOR")` after placing the cursor on the hinge). In Three.js rotate that node directly.
- Blender is Z-up; glTF exports Y-up, and Blender −Y becomes +Z. Model the front of equipment facing −Y so it faces +Z in Three.js.
- Keep segment counts modest (lathe 20–24 steps). A 216 KB transformer dropped to 151 KB just by reducing lathe steps.
- Materials: simple Principled BSDF (base colour, metallic, roughness, emission for lamps). Boost emissive in the loader and set `toneMapped = false` for bloom.

## Export and optimise

- `bpy.ops.export_scene.gltf(export_format="GLB", export_apply=True, export_yup=True, export_cameras=False, export_lights=False)`.
- Optimise with the **libraries** `@gltf-transform/core`, `/extensions`, `/functions` plus `meshoptimizer`: `dedup()`, `weld()`, `prune()`, `meshopt({ encoder, level: "medium" })`. (The `@gltf-transform/cli` package pulled in vulnerable `micromatch/braces`; the libraries do not.)
- Typical results: 850 KB → 150–220 KB per model.

## Loading

- `GLTFLoader` + `MeshoptDecoder` from `three/addons/libs/meshopt_decoder.module.js` — the decoder is embedded, so no CDN request (sites often fetch Draco decoders from a Google CDN; avoid that).
- Load a model only when a zone that uses it is about to be built; cache the loaded scene and clone for instances.
- Record each model in an asset register (source script, licence = own work).

## Verification

- Count and size every GLB after the build; view each zone that uses it in screenshots.
- Confirm named nodes exist (`scene.getObjectByName("Door")`) in a test or at load time.
